## What this letter says
Your son is 14 months old. He was in hospital for Kawasaki disease. The letter says the disease is resolving.
He was treated with high dose aspirin and IVIG. His fever came back within 12 hours of the first IVIG. The IVIG was given again. After the second IVIG, he had no more fever.
Today his fever and rash have completely gone. He has no conjunctivitis (red eyes). He has no redness of the mucous membranes. He is more calm and quiet. He is eating and drinking well.
His echocardiogram (heart scan) was negative.

## What you need to do
1. Give the medicines listed below.
2. If he gets any rash or any fever, go to his primary care doctor as soon as possible.
3. Do not give any vaccine for less than 11 months because of the IVIG. This includes all live virus vaccines.
4. He can be as active as he wants. He can eat and drink as he wants.

## Dates and medicines
- His primary doctor will see him in 2 to 3 days.
- Cardiology (heart doctor) will do a follow-up echo in 4 to 6 weeks.

Medicines:
- Aspirin, high dose: 340 milligrams every 6 hours for 1 day.
- Then aspirin, low dose: 40 milligrams once a day for 14 days.
- Prevacid: 15 milligrams by mouth once a day. It is to protect his stomach and bowel (GI) from the aspirin. The letter does not say how long he takes it.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does IVIG mean?
- What does the echocardiogram show, and what will the next one check?
- How long should he take Prevacid?
- When does the 11 months for vaccines start?

## When to get urgent help
- Any rash or any fever: go to his primary care doctor as soon as possible.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
